readings.title: Consecration of the First-born
readings.subtitle: A Sign Upon the Hand
readings.text: [Exodus 13:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“Set apart to <dn>Me</dn> all the first-born, whatever opens the womb among the children of Yisra’ĕl, both of man and beast; it is <dn>Mine</dn>.”</dq> [3] And Mosheh said to the people, “Remember this day in which you went out of Mitsrayim, out of the house of slavery; for by strength of hand <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> brought you out of this place. And let no leavened bread be eaten. [4] Today you are going out, in the month of Aḇiḇ. [5] And it shall be, when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> brings you into the land of the Kena‘anites, and the Ḥittites, and the Amorites, and the Hiwwites, and the Yeḇusites, which <dn>He</dn> swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, that you shall keep this service in this month. [6] Seven days you eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day is a festival to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [7] Unleavened bread is to be eaten seven days, and let no leavened bread be seen with you, and let no leaven be seen with you within all your border. [8] And you shall inform your son in that day, saying, ‘It is because of what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> did for me when I came up from Mitsrayim.’ [9] And it shall be as a sign to you on your hand and as a reminder between your eyes, that the Torah of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is to be in your mouth, for with a strong hand <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has brought you out of Mitsrayim. [10] And you shall guard this law at its appointed time from year to year. [11] And it shall be, when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> brings you into the land of the Kena‘anites, as <dn>He</dn> swore to you and your fathers, and gives it to you, [12] that you shall pass over to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> every one that opens the womb, and every first-born that comes from any beast, the males belong to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [13] But every first-born of a donkey you shall ransom with a lamb. And if you do not ransom it, then you shall break its neck. And all the first-born of man among your sons you shall ransom. [14] And it shall be, when your son asks you in time to come, saying, ‘What is this?’ that you shall say to him, ‘By strength of hand <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> brought us out of Mitsrayim, out of the house of slavery. [15] ‘And it came to be, when Pharaoh was too hardened to let us go, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> killed all the first-born in the land of Mitsrayim, both the first-born of man and the first-born of beast. Therefore I am slaughtering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> every male that opens the womb, but all the first-born of my sons I ransom.’ [16] And it shall be as a sign on your hand and as frontlets between your eyes, for by strength of hand <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> brought us out of Mitsrayim.”

readings.title: The Path to the Sea
readings.subtitle: The Column of Cloud and Fire
readings.text: [Exodus 13:17] And it came to be, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that <dn>Elohim</dn> did not lead them by way of the land of the Philistines, though that was near; for <dn>Elohim</dn> said, <dq>“Lest the people regret when they see fighting, and return to Mitsrayim.”</dq> [18] So <dn>Elohim</dn> led the people around by way of the wilderness of the Sea of Reeds. And the children of Yisra’ĕl went up armed from the land of Mitsrayim. [19] And Mosheh took the bones of Yosĕph with him, for he had certainly made the children of Yisra’ĕl swear, saying, “<dn>Elohim</dn> shall certainly visit you, and you shall bring my bones up from here with you.” [20] And they departed from Sukkoth and camped in Ětham at the edge of the wilderness. [21] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> went before them by day in a column of cloud to lead the way, and by night in a column of fire to give them light, so as to go by day and night. [22] The column of cloud did not cease by day, nor the column of fire by night, before the people. [Exodus 14:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, that they turn back and camp before Pi Haḥiroth, between Migdol and the sea, opposite Ba‘al Tsephon; camp before it by the sea.</dq> [3] <dq>“For Pharaoh shall say of the children of Yisra’ĕl, ‘They are entangled in the land, the wilderness has closed them in.’</dq> [4] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall harden the heart of Pharaoh, and he shall pursue them. But <dn>I</dn> am to be esteemed through Pharaoh and over all his army, and the Mitsrites shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq> And they did so.

readings.title: Pharaoh’s Pursuit
readings.subtitle: The Fear of Yisra’ĕl
readings.text: [Exodus 14:5] And it was reported to the sovereign of Mitsrayim that the people had fled. And the heart of Pharaoh and his servants was changed toward the people, and they said, “What is this we have done, that we have let Yisra’ĕl go from serving us?” [6] So he made his chariot ready and took his people with him. [7] And he took six hundred chosen chariots, and all the chariots of Mitsrayim, and officers over all of them. [8] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> hardened the heart of Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim, and he pursued the children of Yisra’ĕl. But the children of Yisra’ĕl went out with a high hand. [9] And the Mitsrites pursued them, and all the horses and chariots of Pharaoh, and his horsemen and his army, and overtook them camping by the sea beside Pi Haḥiroth, before Ba‘al Tsephon. [10] And when Pharaoh drew near, the children of Yisra’ĕl lifted their eyes and saw the Mitsrites coming after them. And they were greatly afraid, and the children of Yisra’ĕl cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [11] And they said to Mosheh, “Did you take us away to die in the wilderness because there are no burial sites in Mitsrayim? What is this you have done to us, to bring us up out of Mitsrayim? [12] “Is this not the word that we spoke to you in Mitsrayim, saying, ‘Leave us alone and let us serve the Mitsrites’? For it would have been better for us to serve the Mitsrites than to die in the wilderness.” [13] And Mosheh said to the people, “Do not be afraid. Stand still, and see the deliverance of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which <dn>He</dn> does for you today. For the Mitsrites whom you see today, you are never to see them again, ever. [14] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does fight for you, and you keep silent.”

readings.title: The Dividing of the Waters
readings.subtitle: Deliverance at the Sea
readings.text: [Exodus 14:15] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Why do you cry to <dn>Me</dn>? Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and let them go forward.</dq> [16] <dq>“And you, lift up your rod, and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it, and let the children of Yisra’ĕl go on dry ground through the midst of the sea.</dq> [17] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn>, see, <dn>I</dn> am hardening the hearts of the Mitsrites, and they shall follow them. And <dn>I</dn> am to be esteemed through Pharaoh and over all his army, his chariots, and his horsemen.</dq> [18] <dq>“And the Mitsrites shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, when <dn>I</dn> am esteemed through Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen.”</dq> [19] And the Messenger of <dn>Elohim</dn>, who went before the camp of Yisra’ĕl, moved and went behind them. And the column of cloud moved from before them and stood behind them, [20] and came between the camp of the Mitsrites and the camp of Yisra’ĕl. And it was the cloud and the darkness, and it gave light by night, and the one did not come near the other all night. [21] And Mosheh stretched out his hand over the sea. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea into dry land, and the waters were divided. [22] And the children of Yisra’ĕl went into the midst of the sea on dry ground, and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left. [23] And the Mitsrites pursued and went in after them into the midst of the sea, all the horses of Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen. [24] And it came to be, in the morning watch, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> looked down upon the army of the Mitsrites through the column of fire and cloud, and <dn>He</dn> brought the army of the Mitsrites into confusion. [25] And <dn>He</dn> took off their chariot wheels, so that they drove them with difficulty. And the Mitsrites said, “Let us flee from the face of Yisra’ĕl, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> fights for them against the Mitsrites.” [26] Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Stretch out your hand over the sea, and let the waters come back upon the Mitsrites, upon their chariots, and upon their horsemen.”</dq> [27] And Mosheh stretched out his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to its usual flow at the break of day, with the Mitsrites fleeing into it. So <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> overthrew the Mitsrites in the midst of the sea. [28] And the waters returned and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the army of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them. Not even one of them was left. [29] And the children of Yisra’ĕl walked on dry ground in the midst of the sea, and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left. [30] Thus <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saved Yisra’ĕl that day out of the hand of the Mitsrites, and Yisra’ĕl saw the Mitsrites dead on the seashore. [31] And Yisra’ĕl saw the great work which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had done in Mitsrayim, and the people feared <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and believed in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>His</dn> servant Mosheh.

readings.title: The Song of Mosheh
readings.subtitle: Exaltation of the Deliverer
readings.text: [Exodus 15:1] Then Mosheh and the children of Yisra’ĕl sang this song to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and spoke, saying: “I sing to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>He</dn> is highly exalted! The horse and its rider <dn>He</dn> has thrown into the sea! [2] “<dn>Yah</dn> is my strength and song, and <dn>He</dn> has become my deliverance. <dn>He</dn> is my <dn>Ěl</dn>, and I praise <dn>Him</dn>; <dn>Elohim</dn> of my father, and I exalt <dn>Him</dn>. [3] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is a man of battle, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is <dn>His</dn> Name. [4] “The chariots of Pharaoh and his army <dn>He</dn> has cast into the sea, and his chosen officers are drowned in the Sea of Reeds. [5] “The abyss covered them, they went down to the depths like a stone. [6] “Your right hand, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, has become great in power. <dn>Your</dn> right hand, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, has crushed the enemy. [7] “And in the greatness of <dn>Your</dn> excellence <dn>You</dn> overthrew those who rose against <dn>You</dn>. <dn>You</dn> sent forth <dn>Your</dn> wrath, it consumed them like stubble. [8] “And with the blast of <dn>Your</dn> nostrils the waters were heaped up, the floods stood up like a wall, the depths became stiff in the heart of the sea. [9] “The enemy said, ‘I pursue, I overtake, I divide the spoil, my being is satisfied with them. I draw my sword, my hand destroys them.’ [10] “<dn>You</dn> blew with <dn>Your</dn> wind, the sea covered them, they sank like lead in the mighty waters. [11] “Who is like <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, among the mighty? Who is like <dn>You</dn>, great in set-apartness, awesome in praises, working wonders? [12] “<dn>You</dn> stretched out <dn>Your</dn> right hand, the earth swallowed them. [13] “In <dn>Your</dn> kindness <dn>You</dn> led the people whom <dn>You</dn> have redeemed, in <dn>Your</dn> strength <dn>You</dn> guided them to <dn>Your</dn> set-apart dwelling. [14] “Peoples heard, they trembled, anguish gripped the inhabitants of Philistia. [15] “Then the chiefs of Eḏom were afraid, the mighty men of Mo’aḇ, trembling grips them, all the inhabitants of Kena‘an melted away. [16] “Fear and dread fall on them, by the greatness of <dn>Your</dn> arm they are as silent as a stone, until <dn>Your</dn> people pass over, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, until the people whom <dn>You</dn> have bought pass over. [17] “<dn>You</dn> bring them in and plant them in the mountain of <dn>Your</dn> inheritance, in the place, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which <dn>You</dn> have made for <dn>Your</dn> own dwelling, the set-apart place, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which <dn>Your</dn> hands have prepared. [18] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> reigns forever and ever.” [19] For the horses of Pharaoh went with his chariots and his horsemen into the sea, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> brought back the waters of the sea upon them, and the children of Yisra’ĕl went on dry ground in the midst of the sea. [20] And Miryam the prophetess, the sister of Aharon, took the timbrel in her hand, and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances. [21] And Miryam answered them: “Sing to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>He</dn> is highly exalted! The horse and its rider <dn>He</dn> has thrown into the sea!”

readings.title: The Waters of Marah
readings.subtitle: Testing and Healing
readings.text: [Exodus 15:22] And Mosheh caused Yisra’ĕl to depart from the Sea of Reeds, and they went out into the Wilderness of Shur. And they went three days in the wilderness and found no water. [23] And they came to Marah, but they could not drink the waters of Marah, for they were bitter. Therefore the name of it was called Marah. [24] And the people grumbled against Mosheh, saying, “What are we to drink?” [25] Then he cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> showed him a tree. And when he threw it into the waters, the waters were made sweet. There <dn>He</dn> made a law and a right-ruling for them, and there <dn>He</dn> tried them, [26] and said, <dq>“If you diligently obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> and do what is right in <dn>His</dn> eyes, and shall listen to <dn>His</dn> commands and guard all <dn>His</dn> laws, <dn>I</dn> shall bring on you none of the diseases <dn>I</dn> brought on the Mitsrites, for <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who heals you.”</dq> [27] And they came to Ělim, where there were twelve fountains of water and seventy palm trees. And they camped there by the waters.
